title: exhaust_reference_call.sql never enforces the correction_cycles >= 1 gate its header claims — a first-failure row can be terminalized with a fabricated referee_contact_invalid signal
evidence:
+-- RC4.3 correction-exhaustion terminal (AD-7: one correction cycle; a
+-- second failure converts the row to unreachable). Fired by the delivery
+-- failure sites (email bounce / SMS failure webhooks, wrong-person route)
+-- when the row already ran its correction (correction_cycles >= 1): instead
+-- of returning to awaiting_correction ... the row terminalizes as
+-- unreachable with the referee_contact_invalid fraud signal stamped
+-- (rc3-7's mechanism, LIVE here; the signal is never fabricated).
+WHERE id = $1
+  AND status IN ('queued', 'contact_initiated')
+  -- r2 (BLOCKER): a taken-over row is never exhausted — a redelivered
+  -- bounce must not fabricate referee_contact_invalid on a row the
+  -- landlord is handling (A7).
+  AND taken_over_at IS NULL
+RETURNING id::text;
detail: The WHERE guards states and taken_over_at but has no correction_cycles >= 1 predicate — the one invariant this query exists to protect ('signal is never fabricated') is delegated entirely to callers. The r2 pass hardened every sibling query with SQL-level guards; this one stays caller-gated, and no test exercises a live cycles=0 row against it (exhaustion_guard_only_fires_from_live_states_test only uses a terminal 'objected' row). A regressed or future call site silently terminalizes a never-corrected row and stamps the fraud signal on a contact tried once.
recommended_fix: Add AND correction_cycles >= 1 to the WHERE (it is the AD-7 one-cycle rule, enforceable here), and pin a live cycles=0 row returning 0 rows in exhaustion_guard_only_fires_from_live_states_test.

title: Negative control in payload test is vacuous — asserts an impossible sentinel instead of the actual internal marker
evidence:
-  string.contains(body, "larry@example.com") |> should.be_false
+  // RC4.3 note: the referee's CONTACT snapshot now legitimately rides the
+  // payload (the §7.7 take-over chips + §8.3 edit prefill need it) — the
+  // negative control moved to a still-internal marker (form_token is never
+  // selected by the detail read).
+  string.contains(body, "form_token_internal_sentinel") |> should.be_false
detail: The comment claims the control checks a still-internal marker, but the asserted string 'form_token_internal_sentinel' appears nowhere in the codebase — if form_token (or form_token_expires_at) ever leaked into the detail payload, this test still passes. The control proves nothing.
recommended_fix: Assert absence of the real internal keys, e.g. string.contains(body, "\"form_token\"") |> should.be_false, matching the claimed invariant.

title: stale_pre_correction_failure_stands_down_test uses a fixed absolute timestamp — result depends on the machine clock
evidence:
+      "UPDATE reference_call
+       SET attempts = '[{\"at\":\"2026-08-01T08:00:00Z\",\"channel\":\"email\",\"outcome\":\"delivered\",\"detail\":\"old_send_1\"}]'::jsonb,
+           status = 'awaiting_correction'::reference_call_status
+       WHERE id = $1::uuid",
detail: The test's stand-down assertion depends on corrected_at (now()) being later than '2026-08-01T08:00:00Z'; run before that instant (clock skew, CI replay of the commit), the typed gate classifies the send as post-correction and the row exhausts instead — the test hard-fails. The sibling same-day test uses now()-relative to_char, the robust pattern.
recommended_fix: Write the pre-correction send with to_char(now() - interval '1 hour', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"') like same_day_stale_bounce_stands_down_test.

title: send_is_post_correction casts untrusted jsonb text to timestamptz unguarded — a malformed 'at' value raises and 500s the delivery-failure webhook
evidence:
+       COALESCE((
+         SELECT (e->>'at')::timestamptz >= rc.corrected_at
+         FROM jsonb_array_elements(rc.attempts) AS e
+         WHERE e->>'detail' = $4 AND e->>'outcome' = 'delivered'
+         ORDER BY e->>'at' DESC
+         LIMIT 1
+       ), false) AS send_is_post_correction,
detail: Any delivered attempts entry whose 'at' is not a parseable timestamptz (empty string, bad format) turns the whole find query into an exception, failing the webhook event instead of standing down — the r1 string compare this replaces could never raise. Also note the LIMIT-1 pick still uses lexical ORDER BY e->>'at' while the gate is typed.
recommended_fix: Guard the cast, e.g. CASE WHEN e->>'at' ~ '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T' THEN (e->>'at')::timestamptz >= rc.corrected_at ELSE false END, so malformed history cannot 500 the webhook.
